name: Braided River
desc: A braided gravel-bed river seen from above — water threads scour where the flow concentrates and dump gravel where it slackens, so mid-channel bars build and split the flow into an anastomosing web that re-weaves itself continuously; a bar that grows too tall shoves its own thread aside, floods drown the whole braid and reset it, and low stage re-incises the threads through pale gravel that vegetation is slowly colonising.

energy.doc: transport capacity — how hard the threads scour and how fast bars build — plus colour/contrast gain

scale.doc: magnification into the braid plain around x/y — 1 shows the whole reach, 2.6 crops to a few threads

speed.doc: how fast the braid re-weaves and avulses

density.doc: discharge — number of water parcels, i.e. the braiding index (thread count)

stage.doc: base flow stage: 0 = a starved low-water braid of thin threads on wide bars, 1 = a bank-full flood that drowns the bars

hue.doc: gravel hue anchor; rotates the plate with it

x.doc: view centre x (only bites when scale > 1)

y.doc: view centre y (only bites when scale > 1)

style.doc: aesthetic: aerial = false-colour air photo, silt-blue threads on pale gravel with vegetation taking the old bars; glacial = milky rock-flour meltwater on cold grey outwash; survey = topographic plate; radar = abstracted dark plate where only the wetted braid glows
